How a deal gets here

  1. Collect. The scraper polls the registry feeds (exchange filings, SEC EDGAR, newswires, bank and law-firm newsrooms, trade press) every 2 to 30 minutes.
  2. Filter. It keeps an item only if it has a debt phrase plus a watchlist company or a sector term (data centre, tower, fibre, subsea, satellite, telco).
  3. Extract. It reads the amount, currency, base rate, margin, coupon, tenor, maturity, transaction type, bank roles, legal and financial advisors, and commitment and upfront fees. An LLM extractor does the reading when an API key is set; rule-based extraction runs as a cross-check.
  4. Base rate. When a loan names no benchmark, it shows the market convention for the currency: SOFR, SONIA, EURIBOR, BBSY, TONA, HIBOR, KLIBOR/COF, JIBOR, MCLR or BVAL. These are marked with an asterisk and kept separate from stated rates.
  5. Merge. Reports of the same deal merge into one row, and its status moves from talks to launched, priced, signed and closed.
  6. Alert. New deals and status changes go to Slack or Telegram. Low-confidence rows are held for review.
About this dataset This dataset has 867 deals, put together by researching public sources: company releases, exchange and SEC filings, bank and law-firm announcements, and trade press. Every figure links to its source. Margins, fees and some bank roles sit behind paywalls (IFR, GlobalCapital, LPC), so "Not disclosed" means not public, not zero. Rows marked In talks, In syndication, Sanctioned or Reported are not final and come from press reports. Bitcoin-miner AI builds (CleanSpark, Cipher, Hut 8, IREN, Core Scientific) and SoftBank Group are kept for reference but sit outside the core TMT universe. Searched but no 2026 debt found in public sources: Jio, Indus, MTN, Airtel Africa, Vodacom, SES, Deutsche Telekom, BT, Vodafone, Telkom Indonesia, Axiata, KDDI, SoftBank Corp, the Chinese telcos, e&, Ooredoo, Khazna and G42. Deals by these names may exist behind paywalls (IFR, LPC, GlobalCapital). Microsoft has issued no debt in 2026. 2021 to 2025 are backfilled year by year, with each tranche's maturity taken from SEC filings (424B2, 8-K, 10-K debt notes) for US issuers and from IR bond lists elsewhere, so they feed the refinancing wall. 2021 to 2023 are thinner than later years: some European telco, Gulf, satellite and Africa deals from those years are not yet captured.
Every field links back to a public source in the term sheet.
